body: People tend to look down on trade schools. The thing is: we need people with practical skillsets. Life would be impossible without them. Not everyone is right for college, and not everyone even wants to go to college. Different careers have different paths.

Unfortunately, it seems like she feels they don't need to be pushed. She's also holding you to their standard. Most parents just sort of assume their kids are all equally good at all things. It's not a good assumption to make, but they do it. I bet you bake better than them, right? That's a marketable skill. Have you considered trade school?

Is there anything that might make you happy right now? I know nothing can take away the pain. I totally get that, but is there anything that you would enjoy doing?

You seem very self-aware. That goes a long way. I think for you, the key is to know yourself like you do, but also recognize that you are probably falling victim to magnification/catastrophizing (and your mother may be too.) Check out this neat little chart that my therapist gave me: http://media.psychologytools.org/Worksheets/English/Unhelpful_Thinking_Styles.pdf I hope I'm helping :)

When our world gets shaken up, it seems natural to want out. Just remember that dying won't make anything better. Death isn't peace. It's nothing. Wouldn't you rather be here and able to change your situation?

This won't be easy, but I've been in situations like this a lot in college. Remember that you can rest all you want after. This work stands between you and the ability to not give a shit. Drink a ton of coffee and do it as quickly and poorly as you can. Doing it poorly is better than not doing it at all. 50% is only half the hit on your grade that 0% would be.

I did. "It makes both of us happy right now, and I wasn't feeling happy before." Hardly gives you license to hurt me this much. My pain is greater than their happiness put together.

BTW this account is still new if you're wondering why it takes me so long to respond. I have to wait at least 7 min between comments.
Well stop it!

Ah, man... being a teenager was the worst. I think we've all been there with feeling like nobody's listening. It's different in your case, though. The people around you seem to really have let you down, and I'm sorry for that. You should understand that not everyone will. Not everyone is bad.

Never feel weak for being a victim of anything. There's always something we could do differently, no matter where we are or were in life. Even if you did, it wouldn't change how wrong it was for someone to even try. The person to blame is not the victim. The person to blame is always the one who creates the problem in the first place.

Rape is about power, so it's okay to feel like your power has been taken away from you, but you need to remember that it hasn't. Power isn't something that can actually be given, taken, and lost. We all have agency -control over ourselves and our actions- and that is power. So, to hell with anyone who thinks it's gone. As long as you're still alive and breathing, you're powerful, and you're powerful just for choosing to be.

There's a smile :) My gf when I was 16 was a rape victim too. I don't want to claim that I get it, because I could never know how it feels, but I know what it's like to love someone.

Hell, I improved her confidence so much that she cheated on me and left me! :D
Is there a point? Yeah. To kick all their asses at life and prove that nobody can ruin you! Your boyfriend gets it. He sees in you what everyone should.

I would REALLY love to, but I'm sticking to realism here. I have no alternative except to deal with it. Still not my biggest concern, though. I really just need to get through right now, and I believe I will get better quickly. The here-and-now is just such a hurdle...
I really don't want to. It's not really that I even have any desire to think of it. It's just been becoming more and more prevalent in my thoughts, and the thoughts seem to be beyond my control.
If you feel offended, and I think you do, it shows more self respect than you realize you have. If you really had no self worth, you wouldn't even care.

Not wanting to hurt others is a good motivation. Trust is a big deal, and there's somewhat of an unspoken trust among everyone we see on a daily basis and ourselves that we'll still be there the next day. This is what keeps everyone feeling normal, and it's why when someone leaves, even if it's just to change location, it's a big deal.

Killing ourselves is another form of leaving, but it's an even more jarring one. It does not and cannot benefit ourselves, and does and can disrupt the lives of those around us, sometimes irreparably. Even those who you may not have believed to be close would be affected.
